files.content:
# membership-ledger

The membership ledger for one region. Finance treats it as the record of what
members are owed: `members` holds one row per member, `ledger_entries` is
append-only, `seq` counts a member's own movements and `global_seq` orders the
whole ledger.

## Layout

- `cmd/membershipd` - the service binary
- `internal/api` - the HTTP surface: `/v1/members/...` and `/admin/migration/...`
- `internal/ledger` - what the public endpoints see of the ledger
- `internal/legacy` - the SQLite store a region runs on today
- `internal/store` - client for the storage service
- `internal/migration` - the orchestrator that moves one region's ledger
- `config/migration.yaml` - this deployment's settings

## Running it

```
go build -o membershipd ./cmd/membershipd && ./membershipd
```

Settings are read from `config/migration.yaml`, or from wherever `LEDGER_CONFIG`
points. Every key can be overridden from the environment.

files.content:
# Deployment settings for membershipd.
#
# Every value here differs between deployments and is overridable from the
# environment, so read them rather than assuming them. The environment variable
# for a key is LEDGER_ plus the key in upper case.

listen: 127.0.0.1:8080

# The storage service's socket. It owns the destination database and the
# coordination keyspace.
store_socket: /run/ledger/store.sock

# The legacy store, which is where production traffic still goes.
legacy_path: /app/data/legacy.db

# The clock file the deployment controls. Empty means real time.
clock_file: /run/ledger/clock

# Phase one of the migration copies the ledger as far as this legacy global
# sequence number and no further. It is a property of the cutover plan, not of
# the data, and it is different in every deployment.
shadow_boundary: 500

# How long a migration lease stays valid after it was last written, in seconds
# of the deployment clock.
lease_ttl_seconds: 8

# This worker's identity. Two workers never share one.
lease_holder: membershipd-a

# The largest number of ledger rows to hand the destination store in one write.
apply_batch_max: 200

commits.message:
ci: cache the build cache as well as the modules

The job was passing its ten minute timeout whenever the runner came up cold. modernc.org/sqlite is most of the build and the module cache alone does not help it. Cold runs are about two minutes now; timeout raised to twenty so a cache miss is a slow build and not a red.

Fixes #38
commits.author: mbeaulieu

files.content:
name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: '1.25.0'
      # modernc.org/sqlite is nearly the whole build. The module cache alone
      # does not help it: what costs the ten minutes is compiling it, so the
      # build cache is cached too.
      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cache/go-build
            ~/go/pkg/mod
          key: go-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum') }}
          restore-keys: |
            go-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: build
        run: go build ./...
      - name: vet
        run: go vet ./...
      - name: gofmt
        run: test -z "$(gofmt -l .)"

# ap-2 cutover, archive

The membership ledger in ap-2 was moved off its legacy SQLite store and onto a
destination store by the orchestrator this service is getting. These are the
artefacts that run left behind. They were kept because the remaining regions
have the same move to make.

`deployment.yaml` is ap-2's own `config/migration.yaml`. Its numbers are ap-2's
and no other region's.

## Files

`ledger-export.jsonl`
: ap-2's legacy ledger as exported at retirement, one line per movement.
  `member_id`, `seq`, `global_seq`, `delta_cents`, `reason`, `written_at`.

`member-book.json`
: ap-2's legacy `members` table at retirement. `member_id`, `tier`,
  `balance_cents`, `version`, `deleted`.

`destination-after-shadow-copy.json`, `destination-at-authority-change.json`,
`destination-final.json`
: what the destination store held at three points: when phase one finished,
  at the instant the authority moved, and at the end. `entries` are its ledger
  rows, `members` its member rows, `record` its migration record, `status` the
  service's own `GET /admin/migration/status` where one was taken.

# Deployment settings for membershipd, ap-2, as they were for the cutover.
#
# Kept with the archive because the numbers below are what the recorded run was
# driven with. They are ap-2's; every region sets its own.

listen: 127.0.0.1:8080
store_socket: /run/ledger/store.sock
legacy_path: /app/data/legacy.db
clock_file: /run/ledger/clock

shadow_boundary: 380
lease_ttl_seconds: 15
lease_holder: membershipd-a
apply_batch_max: 200

: ap-2's legacy ledger as exported at retirement, one line per movement.

`migration-record-history.jsonl`
: every version of the migration record the destination store accepted, in the
  order it accepted them. `n` is the position in the store's write log, `conn`
  the connection that wrote it, `was` the record before the write and `became`
  the record after it.

`coordination-keys.jsonl`
: every accepted write to the coordination keyspace, same ordering. `key`,

  is whether it told the caller so. `movements` are the `member_id#seq` a write
  carried. `rows` is how many rows it carried. Positions in the ledger are not
  kept; they were particular to that run.

commits.message:
scripts: a smoke run for a box

Builds, starts the service, drives the admin endpoints and says what it saw. It exists so that a broken build, a service that will not start and a migration that refuses to advance are all obvious without guessing.
commits.author: harun-yildiz

files.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Smoke test: does the migration run at all, and does it survive each of the
# three store mechanics once?
#
#   scripts/smoke.sh            with the smoke faults on
#   scripts/smoke.sh --clean    with no faults, for when you want a baseline
#
# This is here so a broken build, a service that will not start and a migration
# that refuses to advance are all obvious without having to guess. It is not the
# scenario you are graded on: it runs one worker on this box's own data with the
# three fixed smoke faults. Passing it is necessary, not sufficient.
set -uo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1

PORT=${PORT:-8080}
BASE=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT
BIN=/tmp/membershipd-smoke
LOG=/tmp/membershipd-smoke.log
FAULTS=data/smoke-faults

say()  { printf '\nsmoke: %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\nsmoke: FAILED: %s\n' "$*"; exit 1; }

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- the build

say "building"
go build -o "$BIN" ./cmd/membershipd || fail "the build does not compile"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- the box

if [ "${1:-}" = "--clean" ]; then
    rm -f "$FAULTS"
    say "faults off"
else
    : > "$FAULTS"
    say "faults on (fixed: one withheld-committed, one withheld-lost, one kill)"
fi

stop() { pkill -f "$BIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 1; }
stop

say "putting the stores back to a fresh trial"
rm -f data/reset-request.done
touch data/reset-request
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
    [ -f data/reset-request.done ] && break
    sleep 1
done
outcome=$(cat data/reset-request.done 2>/dev/null)
[ "$outcome" = "ok" ] || fail "the reset did not complete cleanly: ${outcome:-no answer}"

start() {
    setsid "$BIN" >> "$LOG" 2>&1 &
    for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
        curl -sf "$BASE/admin/migration/status" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
        sleep 1
    done
    return 1
}

: > "$LOG"
say "starting the service"
start || fail "the service never answered on $BASE (see $LOG)"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- the drive

phase() { curl -sf "$BASE/admin/migration/status" 2>/dev/null | python3 -c \
    'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("phase","?"))' 2>/dev/null; }
field() { curl -sf "$BASE/admin/migration/status" 2>/dev/null | python3 -c \
    "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('$1'))" 2>/dev/null; }

restarts=0
last=$(phase)
say "driving: starting from $last"

for attempt in $(seq 1 60); do
    code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/smoke-advance.json -w '%{http_code}' \
        -X POST "$BASE/admin/migration/advance" 2>/dev/null)

    # One of the smoke faults takes the service down mid-write. That is the
    # mechanic, not a bug in the box.
    if [ -z "$code" ] || [ "$code" = "000" ]; then
        if ! curl -sf "$BASE/admin/migration/status" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            restarts=$((restarts + 1))
            say "the service died during an advance; restarting (#$restarts)"
            start || fail "it did not come back after being killed mid-write (see $LOG)"
            continue
        fi
    fi

    if [ "$code" = "501" ]; then
        fail "advance is not implemented yet — this is the seam to build"
    fi

    now=$(phase)
    if [ "$now" != "$last" ]; then
        printf '  %-16s -> %-16s (http %s)\n' "$last" "$now" "$code"
        last=$now
    fi
    [ "$now" = "COMPLETE" ] && break

    # Refused and going nowhere: either a gate that cannot be met or an advance
    # that is not idempotent. Either way, stop rather than spin.
    if [ "$code" != "200" ] && [ "$code" != "204" ]; then
        if [ "$attempt" -gt 12 ]; then
            fail "stuck in $now: advance keeps returning $code — $(cat /tmp/smoke-advance.json)"
        fi
    fi
done

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- the verdict

final=$(phase)
divergence=$(field divergence_count)
authority=$(field authority)

say "result"
printf '  phase            %s\n'  "$final"
printf '  authority        %s\n'  "$authority"
printf '  divergence_count %s\n'  "$divergence"
printf '  restarts         %s\n'  "$restarts"

[ "$final" = "COMPLETE" ] || fail "the migration ended in $final, not COMPLETE"
[ "$authority" = "destination" ] || fail "the authority is $authority, not destination"
[ "$divergence" = "0" ] || fail "the migration reports $divergence divergence(s) left"

if [ "${1:-}" != "--clean" ] && [ "$restarts" = "0" ]; then
    say "note: nothing was killed mid-write, so one of the three mechanics did
      not actually get exercised on this run."
fi

say "the seam is wired up and the migration completed on this box's data with
      one worker. A graded run is not this."
stop

files.content:
# Migration runbook: legacy ledger to destination store

The plan for moving the membership ledger off the legacy SQLite store and onto
the destination store. ap-2 has already been moved; this region has not.

The orchestrator that carries it out is `internal/migration`, and `Advance` is
not written yet. `config/migration.yaml` holds this deployment's numbers, and
they are this deployment's alone — ap-2 ran on its own, and so will the next
region.

## The two stores

**Legacy** (`internal/legacy`) is the system of record today and production
traffic still goes to it throughout. `members` holds one row per member;
`ledger_entries` is append-only, with `seq` counting a member's own movements
from 1 and `global_seq` ordering the whole ledger.

**Destination** (`internal/store`) is reached through the storage service on a
local socket. It holds members, ledger rows and one migration record. Read
that package's doc comment before you use it: its failure model is not the same
as a database's, and `EntryAdd`, `EntryRemove`, `MetaPut` and `KVCAS` each say
in their own comment what they will and will not do for you.

## Driving it

```
GET  /admin/migration/status    where the migration is, read from the stores
POST /admin/migration/advance   one phase on, if the gate holds
```

`migration.Order` is the phase sequence and `migration.Status` is the report the
tooling that drives a migration expects; both field sets are a contract, so keep
them. Each advance moves the migration on by one phase and only if that phase's
gate holds; an advance that cannot run refuses and changes nothing. Advancing is
driven from outside, may be called again at any time including after a restart,
and there may be more than one process willing to answer.

files.content:
# Migration runbook: legacy ledger to destination store

The plan for moving the membership ledger off the legacy SQLite store and onto
the destination store. ap-2 has already been moved; this region has not.

The orchestrator that carries it out is `internal/migration`, and `Advance` is
not written yet. `config/migration.yaml` holds this deployment's numbers, and
they are this deployment's alone — ap-2 ran on its own, and so will the next
region.

## The two stores

**Legacy** (`internal/legacy`) is the system of record today and production
traffic still goes to it throughout. `members` holds one row per member;
`ledger_entries` is append-only, with `seq` counting a member's own movements
from 1 and `global_seq` ordering the whole ledger.

**Destination** (`internal/store`) is reached through the storage service on a
local socket. It holds members, ledger rows and one migration record. Read
that package's doc comment before you use it: its failure model is not the same
as a database's, and `EntryAdd`, `EntryRemove`, `MetaPut` and `KVCAS` each say
in their own comment what they will and will not do for you.

## Driving it

```
GET  /admin/migration/status    where the migration is, read from the stores
POST /admin/migration/advance   one phase on, if the gate holds
```

`migration.Order` is the phase sequence and `migration.Status` is the report the
tooling that drives a migration expects; both field sets are a contract, so keep
them. Each advance moves the migration on by one phase and only if that phase's
gate holds; an advance that cannot run refuses and changes nothing. Advancing is
driven from outside, may be called again at any time including after a restart,
and there may be more than one process willing to answer.

## What ap-2 left behind

`docs/prior-cutover/` is the archive from the ap-2 run: its ledger export and
member book, the destination store at three points, every version of the
migration record and every coordination key the store accepted, five stretches
of the store's own write log, and a second rehearsal carried by two workers.
It is the only account of a completed migration anyone kept. It is evidence
rather than instructions — nobody wrote up what it means, and ap-2's numbers
are not this deployment's.

## Running it on this box

The storage service will withhold the outcome of a write and will take a writer
down on a durable write. Both happen in production. On this box they are off
until you ask for them:

```
touch data/smoke-faults      # switch the smoke faults on
rm data/smoke-faults         # and off again
```

That installs a fixed set of three, one of each mechanic. The storage service
logs which are in force and which have fired. Only whether the file exists is
read; there is nothing to configure in it.

**These are not the faults a graded run uses, and the graded ones cannot be
arranged from here.** They arrive over a channel the workspace cannot reach, at
positions and in combinations that are not these. Expect more of them, in worse
places, and expect them to overlap with each other and with a second worker.
The smoke faults are here to tell you that your service is wired up and that it
survives each mechanic once. Passing them is not the same as being right.

## Starting over

A migration is a one-way trip, so trying one twice needs the box put back
first:

```
touch data/reset-request
```

Within a second or two the destination store is emptied, the coordination
keyspace is flushed, and `data/legacy.db` goes back to how it shipped;
`data/reset-request.done` then says `ok` or what went wrong. The smoke faults go
back on afterwards if they were on before. Stop the service first — a reset
underneath a running migration is not worth reasoning about.

What is in this one:

- `migration.Order` and `migration.Status`: the phase sequence and the shape `/admin/migration/status` answers with. Both field sets are what the tooling reads.
- `config/migration.yaml`, with a comment on every key and `LEDGER_` overrides from the environment.
- `GET /v1/members/{id}/ledger` returns every row for a member instead of the first hundred (#43).
- The build job caches the Go build cache as well as the module cache, which is #38 closed.

`migration.Orchestrator.Advance` still reports `ErrNotImplemented` in this tree.

issues.title: ci: the build job times out about one run in five
issues.body:
The build job on the shared runner goes red about one run in five and always the same way: `go build ./...` passes the ten minute job timeout and the runner kills it. A rerun is green.

modernc.org/sqlite is nearly all of it. Warm module cache: 90 seconds. Cold: over eight minutes twice this week, and both reds were cold.

Three reds since Monday. Nothing to do with the changes in them.

comments.body: Two more overnight, both on #39, both on a cold runner. Timings from the logs: 8m41s and 9m58s, killed at ten.

Raising the timeout on its own would only hide it. The module cache is already cached and does not help - what costs the ten minutes is compiling sqlite, so the build cache is the thing to keep. Happy for someone to take it, otherwise I will after the config work lands.
Build cache cached on main. Eleven green runs in a row since, cold runs about two minutes. Closing.

issues.title: docs: say where a deployment's numbers come from
issues.body:
Third person this month has asked me which numbers in this service are the code's and which are the region's, and there is nowhere to point them.

What I would like written down where a new starter will find it: which file holds them, that the environment can override them, and that one region's numbers are not another's.

comments.body: #42 puts `config/migration.yaml` in the tree with a comment on every key, including that the values differ between deployments and are read rather than assumed. That is the file to point people at.
Good enough for now - the comments say it and the loader matches them. Closing. It wants folding into a runbook when there is one.

issues.title: GET /v1/members/{id}/ledger returns at most 100 entries
issues.body:
The reconciliation job reads this endpoint per member. For members with a long history the total it computes disagrees with `balance_cents` from the member read.

One member here has 240 movements. The endpoint answers with 100 of them: no count, no `next`, nothing that says it stopped early. So the two endpoints disagree with each other and the job believes the one that is short.

We found it because month end was light for exactly the members with the longest histories.

comments.body: It is a `LIMIT 100` in `Store.Ledger`, there since the endpoint was first written. The scan the migration uses is a different query and keeps its limit. PR shortly.
Re-ran reconciliation against the fix on a copy: totals match the member reads for every member we were short on. Thank you.

issues.title: ap-2: member reads slowed to seconds during the cutover run
issues.body:
Writing down what on-call saw during the ap-2 run before it goes with the box.
This has been in a thread and a text file since; putting it on a ticket so the
archive PR has something to point at.

Times are the deployment clock's, off the service log and the storage service's
own log. This is a latency report, not a correctness one.

- 18:31 - run started, phase INIT. `GET /v1/members/{id}` p99 was 40 ms.
- 18:33 - SHADOW_COPY. p99 climbed to about 380 ms and stayed there for the copy.
- 18:44 - CATCH_UP. Two support tickets in six minutes, both "the page is
  spinning". The slowest read we have a trace for is 41 s. It completed.
- 18:45 - the storage service log shows its socket accept queue full for roughly
  a minute either side.
- 18:52 - RECONCILE. p99 back under 100 ms.
- 18:58 - the authority moved. No tickets after this point.
- 19:10 - the run finished.

ap-2 was driven with `apply_batch_max: 200` and `lease_ttl_seconds: 15`; its
settings file is going into the archive as `deployment.yaml`. Those are ap-2's
numbers, not this region's.

comments.body: Finance re-ran the month-end reconciliation afterwards against the export and the totals match the legacy book. Recording that here so it is on the ticket rather than in my mail.
Do we have the storage service's log from that window, or only the service's? Asking because the accept-queue line above is the only thing we have from the store side.
We have the write log, which is 40 MB. #46 takes five stretches of it. The rest goes with the box.

The artefacts from that run are archived now (#46, #47). The timeline above is what was seen and the files are where anyone can read them; nobody has written up what they mean. Closing this one - it is a latency report and the box it describes is gone.

issues.title: docs/prior-cutover: the questions the files leave open
issues.body:
Collecting what the archive does not say, so it is in one place for whoever
eventually sits down with it. Not asking anyone to answer these now.

- `coordination-keys.jsonl`: every line carries an `op` and the MANIFEST does
  not mention it. Same for `store-write-log-extracts.jsonl`.
- `open-ledger-probe.json`: the MANIFEST talks about a top-level `member_id`
  that the file does not have.
- `handover-turns.json`: the paragraph describes the file but not the fields in
  `turns`, and one of the eight turns has a field none of the others do.
- `destination-at-authority-change.json`: no `status` block where the other two
  dumps have one. The MANIFEST hedges this with "where one was taken", so it is
  covered, but it is the kind of thing that reads as a missing file.

None of it is wrong exactly, it is undescribed. Sub-issue for the two that are
one-line edits.

comments.body: The `status` one caught me out too - I went looking for the file that had been truncated before I read the MANIFEST properly.
That one I can answer: nobody took a status at that point in the run. That dump came off the store directly.

issues.title: MANIFEST: `op` is undescribed, and the probe's member_id is not where it says
issues.body:
Two one-line edits to `docs/prior-cutover/MANIFEST.md`, both raised in review on
#46 and #47 and both still open:

- The `coordination-keys.jsonl` paragraph names `key`, `value` and `swapped`.
  Every line also has an `op` and the paragraph does not mention it.
  @nadia-okafor said on #46 that it is the store's own name for the write and
  that she would rather not describe it from a guess, which is fair.
- The `open-ledger-probe.json` paragraph says `member_read` and `ledger_read`
  are for the member in `member_id`. There is no top-level `member_id` in that
  file; it is `member_read.body.member_id`.

I have not touched the file myself. It is an archive, and I would rather the
edit came from whoever captured it.

issues.title: a make target for the smoke run
issues.body:
Four commands get typed around `scripts/smoke.sh` every time: build, check the storage service is up, run the script, tail its log. A `make smoke` doing the four would save the typing and stop three people keeping three variants of it in their shell history.

Low priority, and I am not volunteering this month.

comments.body: A Makefile would want the storage service path in it, which differs per box. Doable, just not free. Happy to take it if nobody else does.

pulls.title: ledger: the view the public endpoints ask
pulls.body:
The handlers were reaching into `internal/legacy` directly. This puts `ledger.View` between them and the store, with `LegacyView` behind it.

No behaviour change: the endpoints just stop knowing which store answered them.

reviews.body: Clean seam and the handlers read better for it. One naming note inline, not blocking.

review_comments.body: `LegacyView.Ledger` reads the member first and throws the result away. That is deliberate - it is how the endpoint gets its 404 - but it reads like a stray call. A one-line comment would save the next reader.

comments.body: `ci / build` was red on the first push and green on a rerun. That is #38, not this branch.

pulls.title: migration: the phase order and the status shape
pulls.body:
`migration.Order`, `migration.Status`, and `Next`/`Index` over the order.

`Advance` is a stub reporting `ErrNotImplemented`. This PR is the names and the report only: the tooling team wanted the JSON to build against and this is it. Both field sets are a contract with that tooling.

reviews.body: Names look right to me and the doc comments say what each of them is. Not approving because I have not seen the tooling's side of it.
Tooling side matches: we read `phase`, `authority`, `cursor` and the two legacy counts. Approving on the JSON.

review_comments.body: `Order` being a `var` and not a `const` slice is unavoidable in Go, but nothing stops a caller reordering it. Not worth a copy on every read; noting it so nobody is surprised.
`Index` returning -1 for an unknown phase is fine, please say so in the comment - it does, ignore me.

pulls.title: config: the deployment settings membershipd reads
pulls.body:
`config/migration.yaml`, with a comment on every key saying what it is and that it differs between deployments. `internal/config` already reads it and takes `LEDGER_` plus the key in upper case from the environment.

The values in the file are this deployment's. Nothing outside `internal/config` reads the file.

Closes #41.

reviews.body: The comments are the useful part of this file. One question inline that does not block it.

review_comments.body: Every other key here has an `LEDGER_` override in the loader. `apply_batch_max` does not. Deliberate, or an oversight?
`store_socket` under `/run` means the directory has to exist before the service starts. Worth a line in the README rather than another comment here.

comments.body: Leaving `apply_batch_max` as it is for now.

pulls.title: legacy: return every ledger row for a member
pulls.body:
`Store.Ledger` had a `LIMIT 100` on it from when the endpoint was first written, and nothing above it said the answer was partial: a member with more than a hundred movements got the first hundred and no marker.

`EntriesAfter` keeps its explicit limit - that scan is paged by its caller and wants one.

Response shape is untouched. Fixes #43.

reviews.body: Checked a member with 240 movements against a copy of the ledger: all 240 come back, in `seq` order, and the reconciliation total matches the member read.

review_comments.body: Ordering by `seq` here rather than `global_seq` is what the endpoint documents, so this is right. Say so in a comment and the next reader does not have to check.

comments.body: Deliberately not adding `?limit=` and `?after=` here. The response shape is what the reconciliation job and two dashboards read, and I do not want to change it in a bug fix.

pulls.title: docs: archive what the ap-2 cutover left behind
pulls.body:
ap-2 is off its legacy store. The box it ran on is being decommissioned at the
end of the month and everything on it goes with it, so this puts the run's
artefacts in the repo where the regions that have not moved can read them.

What is here and how it was captured:

- `deployment.yaml` - a copy of ap-2's own `config/migration.yaml`, taken off
  the box as it stood for the run. Its numbers are ap-2's.
- `ledger-export.jsonl` - the legacy ledger exported at retirement, one line per
  movement, in `global_seq` order.
- `member-book.json` - the legacy `members` table at the same moment.
- `destination-after-shadow-copy.json`, `destination-at-authority-change.json`,
  `destination-final.json` - the destination store dumped through the storage
  service's admin dump at three points. Two of them also carry the service's own
  `GET /admin/migration/status` as it answered at the time; the middle one does
  not, because nobody took one.
- `migration-record-history.jsonl`, `coordination-keys.jsonl` - read out of the
  storage service's write log: every accepted write to the migration record and
  to the coordination keyspace, in the order the store took them.
- `store-write-log-extracts.jsonl` - five stretches of that same log, grouped by
  window. The whole log is 40 MB and most of it is the copy, so only the
  stretches somebody looked at during the run are kept.

`MANIFEST.md` describes the files and their columns. It does not say what any of
it means and neither does this PR: it is the run's evidence, kept because the
other regions have the same move to make.

About half a megabyte in total, the three destination dumps most of it.

reviews.body: Read this as a document rather than as data - I have not opened the big three. The MANIFEST is clear about most of it. Two naming notes and one column I could not work out, inline. None of them block.

Fine to land. Evidence with a manifest beats evidence in a home directory on a box that is about to be wiped. The `op` question can be answered later by whoever knows; it is not worth holding the PR for.

review_comments.body: This paragraph names `key`, `value` and `swapped`. Every line in the file also carries an `op`, which is not described anywhere here - I can guess from the values but I would rather not have to.
The file name says what it is not: on the box this is `config/migration.yaml`. The header comment covers it and renaming an archived file is worse, so leave it - I just read it twice.

This is in `global_seq` order but `written_at` does not climb with it - line 1 is 17:46:47 and there are lines much further down that are earlier than that. Worth a sentence in the MANIFEST so the next reader does not think the file is corrupt.
`after-shadow-copy` / `at-authority-change` / `final`: three naming shapes for three files of the same kind. Not worth a rename now the paths are in the MANIFEST and in the PR body.

comments.body: Answered what I could in the MANIFEST. `op` is the store's own name for the write and I have left it as the exporter emitted it; I did not write the exporter and I am not going to describe it from a guess.
The service that carried ap-2 ran off a branch on that box and the branch went with the box. What is in this PR is what was recoverable.
The two probes and the rehearsal turns are not in here - they were captured on a second box and I am still getting them off it. Follow-up PR rather than holding this one.
Please keep `ledger-export.jsonl` exactly as exported. Finance reconciled against that file and I would like the bytes we reconciled against to be the bytes in the repo.

pulls.title: docs: the ap-2 probes and the rehearsal turns
pulls.body:
The rest of the ap-2 material, off the second box.

- `dual-read-probe.json` - one member read through the public API while the
  destination was still behind, with the ledger's own numbers for that member at
  that instant and both stores' rows for them. Captured with curl against the
  running service; `status` is what `/admin/migration/status` answered in the
  same breath.
- `open-ledger-probe.json` - the same member read again later in the run, with
  an adjustment written for a different member and the reply it got.
- `handover-turns.json` - the second region-wide rehearsal, carried by two
  workers through a rolling deployment: every advance either worker attempted,
  the phase it went from and to, and the lease record after each turn.

MANIFEST extended to cover the three. I have described the fields and not what
they show - I was not on the call.

reviews.body: Thanks for chasing the second box. Descriptions match what is in the files as far as I checked.

review_comments.body: This paragraph says `member_read` and `ledger_read` are for the member in `member_id`. There is no top-level `member_id` in the file - it is inside `member_read.body`. Not asking you to fix it in this PR.
Eight turns and one of them has no `to` and no `http_status`. Assuming that is what the file recorded and not something lost in transit?

comments.body: It is what the file recorded - that entry has `died` on it instead. I have left it exactly as captured.

`docs / link-check` is red on the three new `.jsonl` and `.json` paths - it only follows links to Markdown. Merging over it; #46 tripped the same check and it was green there only because the MANIFEST links were the last thing it looked at.
Fine. I will open a docs ticket for the MANIFEST wording rather than have you edit an archive in a PR that is adding to it.

pulls.title: docs: runbook - the archive, the smoke faults, the reset

reviews.body: Reads as what it is. Two notes inline, neither blocking.

review_comments.body: The two shell blocks use paths relative to the workspace root and the surrounding prose does not say so. It is obvious from the next paragraph; mentioning it in case you want to be explicit.
Bold line where the other sections use a heading. Fine by me, just inconsistent with the rest of the file.

comments.body: Worth linking #48 from the archive section? Whoever reads the runbook is the person who will hit those gaps.

Left it out. The runbook says where the files are; the ticket is a list of things I could not describe, and I do not want the doc to read as if the archive is half-broken. It is complete, it is just undescribed.
